summary: Redwood AE + SE walked ZenWellness through the Console's request playback, tracing UI, and error analysis workflows. Customer is evaluating for a pilot focused on short-form content generation behind SSO and VPC constraints. Main asks: exportable traces, how fallback policies work, quantization and latency tradeoffs, and what logs are retained for compliance.
topics: Security: SSO, KMS, VPC, audit logs
transcript:
Meeting Header: 2025-11-05 15:00 PST · Duration 62 mins · Attendees listed above

Summary (auto): Quick demo of Console playback and debugging flows. Showed trace waterfall, token-level latency spikes, and where Redwood suggests batching/caching. Customer asked about data residency and audit extracts.

[00:00] Alex Rivera: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, happy to kick off. I see Nina, Tom, Priya — hi. Can you hear us okay?
[00:08] Nina Cho: Yes, sounds good. We got your invite, thanks. Marcus seems to be on... volume is low for him though.
[00:14] Alex Rivera: Awesome. Brief agenda — Console playback, request logs, tracing waterfall, error analysis, then Q&A and next steps. Samir will drive the trace demo.
[00:24] Samir Patel: Cool. I'm going to share my screen, you'll see the Console with a sample request history. I'm pulling up a recent example where we saw a retry followed by an unexpected 'empty' generation.
[00:35] [screen share starts]
[00:40] Samir Patel: The request inspector shows the request ID, model variant, token counts, and the per-token latency line. You can expand to see kernel selection notes — sometimes it shows 'int8 path' or quantized variant.
[00:57] Tom Alvarez: Quick q: that kernel selection — is that deterministic or does it change mid-rollout? We had a weird case where throughput dipped.
[01:06] Samir Patel: Good question. It can change based on sequence length and load; runtime picks the kernel that best matches. For Dedicated you can pin quantization profiles if you want stable behavior.
[01:18] Nina Cho: When you say 'pin', do you mean at model-version level or route level?
[01:23] Samir Patel: Model-version level today, route-level pinning is on the roadmap but not GA.
[01:30] Priya Singh: We need to make sure our compliance folks get audit-friendly exports. How long do you keep request logs and traces?
[01:38] Alex Rivera: Hosted by default is 90 days, but for Dedicated or Private you can set retention via the Console and we can enable longer audit retention in the enterprise package. We can produce CSV/JSON exports of traces.
[01:50] Nina Cho: Can you show an export?
[01:52] Samir Patel: Yup — going to the trace, selecting 'Export trace', here's the payload. Note: the exported KV cache entries are redacted by default unless the customer opts in — we show metadata about cache hits/misses.
[02:10] [00:02:10] Samir Patel: Also worth calling out — the Console highlights 'error buckets' and suggests likely causes. In this case the error was an early EOS triggered by a malformed system prompt.
[02:21] Marcus (muted, low audio): ...sorry can you repeat EOS?
[02:24] Nina Cho: End-of-sequence.
[02:26] Samir Patel: Right, EOS early. The error analysis view maps the token span where the model emitted EOS and shows preceding tokens and prompt metadata so you can repro quickly.
[02:38] Tom Alvarez: Is that mapping automatic or does it rely on instrumentation in our client? We might not be sending full prompt content to hosted logs for privacy.
[02:48] Alex Rivera: You can configure redaction rules on the Console — certain fields are never stored, some are hashed. For Private deployments you can keep full fidelity on-prem.
[02:57] Nina Cho: We're mixed — some PII-free prompts are okay, but user PII must not leave our VPC. So Private or VPC-hosted Dedicated is likely.
[03:06] Samir Patel: Makes sense. For a pilot we often set up a VPC-connected Dedicated pool so the control plane still runs but inference nodes are in the customer's VPC — that gives you flow logs and KMS control.
[03:20] [00:03:20] Samir Patel: Back to the request playback — you can replay a request against a different model variant in the Console; it spawns a synthetic request and shows token-by-token diff to help with regression debugging.
[03:35] Priya Singh: That sounds useful. Does replay count as billable usage?
[03:39] Alex Rivera: Replays in the Console incur minimal compute costs and are tracked — we show them in the cost dashboard and you can exclude them from billing in Dedicated pilot agreements.
[03:48] Nina Cho: Show us the waterfall.
[03:50] Samir Patel: Here — waterfall view. Each span is color-coded: model inference, KV lookups, tokenizer time, and I/O. You can hover to see exact ms and the node that executed it.
[04:03] Tom Alvarez: The spike at token 42 — can you explain?
[04:07] Samir Patel: That was a cache miss followed by a long matrix multiplication because the sequence forced a different kernel. The trace notes 'high memory pressure' on that node; you can see the node ID and we can correlate with infra metrics.
[04:22] Nina Cho: How do you correlate traces with infra metrics? Do you integrate with Prometheus / Datadog?
[04:27] Samir Patel: Yes — Console links to metrics and can push span IDs to Datadog or our tracing backend. We have a built-in exporter and a Datadog/OpenTelemetry connector.
[04:36] [00:04:36] Alex Rivera: Quick interjection — on the Optimize side we surface recommendations: batching to lower per-token tail latency, and prefix caching suggestions when your route has repeated context. We can run our analyzer on a trace sample and give a one-page playbook.
[04:54] Nina Cho: Can you run that analyzer against our sample corpus? We have a lot of repeated headings and small prompts, so batching might help.
[05:02] Samir Patel: For sure — that's one of Samir's tasks to run the analyzer. We'll need a redacted sample of ~1k requests and target latencies.
[05:11] Priya Singh: On security — SSO, SAML, SCIM, can you show where that is in the Console?
[05:16] [screen: settings] Samir Patel: Under Org settings — you can configure SAML IdP, SCIM provisioning, role-based access controls. Audit logs are under 'Security & Compliance' with export buttons.
[05:28] Tom Alvarez: Does your audit log contain the full prompt or only hashes?
[05:31] Samir Patel: Depends on config. By default for hosted we hash sensitive fields. For Dedicated we can keep raw prompts in the VPC under customer control.
[05:41] [00:05:41] Nina Cho: A couple of practical items: if we do a pilot, can we get a per-route SLA for latency? Our product needs sub-300ms 95th for short prompts.
[05:52] Alex Rivera: We can commit to latency SLOs for Dedicated and Enterprise plans with agreed workload profiles. Part of pilot sizing will be to validate that with load tests.
[06:00] Samir Patel: We'll run a targeted benchmark — I recommend starting with 50 RPS and measure p95 under 1k concurrent contexts; then we tune batching and node sizing.
[06:10] Marcus: audio low... I think we asked about error classification — do you have auto-labeling or is it manual?
[06:18] Samir Patel: Auto-labeling — model emits a status and Console maps to buckets (timeout, EOS, rate-limit, infra error). We also show 'suspected cause' with confidence score; sometimes it's noisy but helpful.
[06:31] Marcus: okay thanks.
[06:34] [00:06:34] Alex Rivera: Quick detour — pricing. For pilots we normally give credits and trial terms; I'll send the pricing and Dedicated sizing worksheet after this.
[06:45] Nina Cho: Please include headroom guidance — our infra team is sensitive to burst costing.
[06:49] Alex Rivera: Will do.
[06:51] [screen: request playback demo continues]
[06:56] Samir Patel: Now I'm going to simulate a replay against a quantized int8 variant. Console shows token diffs in red when outputs change; you can also toggle to see only semantic diffs.
[07:12] Tom Alvarez: If quantization causes occasional hallucination, do you have rollback/fallback policies?
[07:17] Samir Patel: Yes — routing policies can be set to fallback to a higher-precision variant on errors or quality regressions. You can also set canary percentages for rollouts.
[07:27] Nina Cho: How are rollouts monitored? Does Console alert on quality regression automatically?
[07:32] Alex Rivera: We support evals against your prompt sets and can fire alerts when metrics cross thresholds. Evals are versioned and tied to rollout policies.
[07:41] [00:07:41] Priya Singh: Any gotchas with VPC networking? We need to ensure no egress to public internet from inference nodes.
[07:49] Samir Patel: For private/Dedicated VPC we support strict egress controls and static egress IPs for partner integrations. We can also deploy on-prem if needed.
[07:59] Tom Alvarez: Good. Next, what's the smallest pilot you recommend?
[08:03] Alex Rivera: A focused pilot: 1-2 routes, 1 model version, 4-8 GPUs for two weeks — enough to validate latency and costs. We'll instrument traces and run Optimize suggestions.
[08:15] Nina Cho: Sounds reasonable. Who will be the primary SE contact?
[08:19] Alex Rivera: Samir will be the SE lead. I'll coordinate next steps and legal. Jordan in CS will help with onboarding.
[08:27] [00:08:27] Alex Rivera: Let's go into a sample error bucket — this one labeled 'prompt-truncation'. You can open any request and see the prompt length, tokenization, and whether it was truncated at the client or server.
[08:40] Samir Patel: The UI has a toggle to show 'client-truncation hints' — if the client library trimmed the prompt, we show where it cut off. That helps reduce support back-and-forth.
[08:52] Marcus: that's neat.
[08:54] [00:08:54] Nina Cho: Any limitations around request playback for streamed responses? We rely on streaming for user-facing latency.
[09:02] Samir Patel: Streamed responses can be replayed as well; the Console reconstructs the event sequence. For debugging we show partial token timings and the stream frames.
[09:12] Tom Alvarez: Do you support function calling telemetry? We use that heavily.
[09:16] Samir Patel: Yes — function call events are captured, and we include arguments and return artifacts in the trace (subject to redaction rules).
[09:25] Alex Rivera: Time check — 15 mins left. Any more big topics?
[09:29] Priya Singh: One more: retention for audit logs we talked about — for SOC2 we need 1 year. Is that feasible?
[09:35] Alex Rivera: For Dedicated/Private yes; Hosted can be extended via an add-on. We'll detail options in the security doc.
[09:43] Nina Cho: Great. Can you email the trace export example and the Optimize one-pager?
[09:48] Alex Rivera: Absolutely.
[09:50] [00:09:50] Samir Patel: Final demo note — the Console's 'auto-suggest' will recommend batching keys and where to insert prefix caching. It even gives expected cost delta percent.
[10:03] Tom Alvarez: That cost delta is critical for us. Please show historical before/after in the pilot.
[10:09] Alex Rivera: We can provide that in the pilot report.
[10:12] Nina Cho: Thanks, this was useful. Next step: we'll confirm pilot routes and share sample logs.
[10:17] Alex Rivera: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the artifacts and schedule the security call.
[10:22] [closing small talk — off topic]
